mechanism_narrative: The steep fall in WORKPLACES mobility is a leading indicator of weaker weekday foot traffic and fewer discretionary errands, so RETAIL_REC will stay below its recent 4-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rebounds to near baseline while RETAIL_REC still averages lower than the prior 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its recent level, people substitute home-based activity for shopping trips, so retail visits weaken within one week and RETAIL_REC declines further.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points for at least 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated but RETAIL_REC does not fall week-on-week within the next 7 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES compresses commuting-linked shopping opportunities, so retail-and-recreation mobility falls more than it would from either series alone over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed but RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 14 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp deterioration in PARKS mobility reflects broad activity suppression and tighter crowd avoidance, which spills over into lower retail mobility over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -10 points and remains there for 2 weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -10 while RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 28-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates precautionary stocking and essential-trip substitution, which crowds out discretionary shopping and pulls RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If retail mobility falls while residential time stays elevated, the pattern signals substitution toward at-home consumption rather than out-of-home spending, keeping RETAIL_REC weak within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC drops more than 5 points while RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC falls below the trigger while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated yet retail mobility reverses upward within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from its recent low should restore access to shopping districts and support higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, especially if WORKPLACES also stops weakening.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 5 points from its latest weekly mean
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rebounds by at least 5 points and RETAIL_REC still averages lower than the prior 28 days over the next month, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-tightening regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and PARKS captures broad movement suppression, and retail mobility should decline within one week as discretionary trips are cut first.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and PARKS remain weak but RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the regime-conditional mechanism is rejected.
